cards.name: Pendulum Random
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: sliders for a pendulum swing (rotation that oscillates and dies away) that re-triggers at random intervals. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on Rotation reads it.
use_for: Make a hanging lower-third tag or price tag swing now and then
Idle sway on a hanging icon or sticker in an explainer
Playful random wobble on a cut-out character head in a satire reel
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing; a script that only adds the effect reports success with no visible change
Large Amplitude on text reads as cheap and hurts legibility

params.name: Decay
params.does: How fast each swing dies out

params.name: Min Delay
params.does: Shortest gap in seconds before the next random swing

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Pendulum Random'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): on Transform/Rotation: var c=effect("Pendulum Random"),A=c("Amplitude"),f=c("Frequency"),k=c("Decay"),lo=c("Min Delay").value,hi=c("Max Delay").value;seedRandom(index,true);var t0=0,t1=random(lo,hi);while(t1<=time){t0=t1;t1+=random(lo,hi);}var t=time-t0;value+A*Math.sin(2*Math.PI*f*t)*Math.exp(-k*t); Move the Anchor Point to the hanging point (top centre) first or the layer spins around its middle. No Premiere equivalent.

cards.name: Percentage Controls
cards.summary: Control panel for AE's 'Percentage Counter Monospaced' text preset: an animatable number plus formatting options that the preset's Source Text expression turns into a counting percentage such as 0% to 72%. On its own it shows nothing.
use_for: Animated poll or vote-share figure counting up in a political explainer
GDP, inflation or growth-rate callouts in news reels
Progress or completion percentage in an AI-education explainer
avoid: Adding the effect alone does nothing: the counter only works through the shipped preset
Pad Zeros defaults to 3, so 72 shows as 072%: set it to 1 (or the final digit count)
Count-ups longer than ~3 s feel slow in reels

params.name: Animate Value
params.does: The number shown; keyframe it to count
params.typical: 0 to the final figure over 1-2 s

params.name: 10x Value Multiplier
params.does: Power-of-ten multiplier: shown number = Animate Value x 10^(value-1); 1 = as typed

params.name: Pad Zeros
params.does: Minimum number of integer digits (pads with leading zeros): default 3 turns 72 into 072%
params.typical: 1 for no padding, or the digit count of the final figure

params.name: Percent Symbol Scale
params.does: Size of the % sign relative to the digits

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (PresetEffects.xml). Do not add it by match name: apply the preset file 'Support Files/Presets/Text/Number Counters/Percentage Counter Monospaced.ffx' to a TEXT layer with layer.applyPreset(File(path)); it adds this effect (instance renamed 'Percentage Counter Controls') plus a Source Text expression (Intl.NumberFormat) and text animators (CharacterOffset, RepositionNonNumbers, AddGroupedSpacing, RepositionCenterOffset, RepositionPercentSymbol) that read the controls BY INDEX, so never rename, reorder or delete its properties. Address it by match name ('Pseudo/ADBE Percentage Controls'), not by display name, then keyframe 'Animate Value' (UI slider stops at 100 but values to +/-1,000,000 can be set; the digits use its absolute value). Read from the preset's expressions: Pad Zeros = minimum integer digits; 10x Value Multiplier shifts the shown number by powers of ten (leave at 1); Number Format 1/2/3 = en-US / de-DE / fr-FR grouping; Show Group Separators toggles grouping. Use a monospaced or tabular-figure font so digits do not jitter. No Premiere equivalent (use a mogrt built in AE).

verified.note: Card status is hidden (control-only pseudo effect with no visible output of its own), so no gallery frame was rendered and none is in the index.

cards.name: Pulse
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: sliders for a scale 'pop' that jumps and settles back, optionally repeating every Cycle Time seconds. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on Scale reads it.
use_for: Pop a key word, logo or icon on its first frame
Repeating heartbeat pulse on a 'LIVE' or 'BREAKING' badge
Attention bump on a subscribe/CTA button in reels
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing
Large Amplitude upscales footage past 100% (soft pixels); negative Amplitude shrinks it and exposes the layer edges
Constant pulsing on body text is tiring to read

params.name: Delay
params.does: Seconds after the layer's in-point before the pop

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Pulse'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): on Transform/Scale: var c=effect("Pulse"),A=c("Amplitude"),k=c("Decay"),cy=c("Cycle Time");var t=time-inPoint-c("Delay");if(cy>0&&t>0)t=t%cy;var s=t<0?0:A*Math.exp(-k*t);value+[s,s]; Simpler shipped alternative: apply the preset 'Scale Bounce - layer markers.ffx' (Presets/Behaviors) and put one layer marker at the pop (its bump eases up before and down after the marker). No Premiere equivalent (keyframe Motion > Scale).

cards.name: Pulse At Marker
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: sliders for a scale pop that fires at each layer marker and settles back. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on Scale reads it.
use_for: Pop a graphic on each narration emphasis by dropping layer markers
Beat-synced pops on icons or stickers in reels (markers on the beats)
Hit each bullet point as the voice-over names it
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing
No layer markers means no pop
Markers too close together stack pops into jitter

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: Peak extra scale in percent at each marker

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Pulse At Marker'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): on Transform/Scale: var c=effect("Pulse At Marker"),s=0;if(marker.numKeys>0){var n=marker.nearestKey(time).index;if(marker.key(n).time>time)n--;if(n>0){var t=time-marker.key(n).time;s=c("Amplitude")*Math.exp(-c("Decay")*t);}}value+[s,s]; The script must also add layer markers: layer.property('Marker').setValueAtTime(t, new MarkerValue('')). Simpler shipped alternative: apply the preset 'Scale Bounce - layer markers.ffx' (Presets/Behaviors) instead (symmetric bump centred on each marker, not a decaying pop). No Premiere equivalent.

cards.name: Pulse On Beat
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: sliders plus an audio-layer picker for a scale pop that fires whenever an audio amplitude track crosses a threshold. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on Scale reads it.
use_for: Logo or title that thumps on the kick drum of a trailer score
Reel stickers or emojis popping to the music beat
Audio-reactive badge on a podcast or news-clip visualiser
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing
Needs a 'Convert Audio to Keyframes' layer; dialogue-heavy audio triggers constantly
Threshold too low gives continuous jitter

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: Peak extra scale in percent per beat

params.name: Audio Threshold
params.does: Amplitude level that counts as a beat (units of the Audio Amplitude slider)
params.typical: a little under the kick peaks, often 10-25

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Pulse On Beat'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): on Transform/Scale: var c=effect("Pulse On Beat"),A=c("Amplitude"),k=c("Decay"),th=c("Audio Threshold"),s=c("Audio Keyframe Layer").effect("Both Channels")("Slider"),f=thisComp.frameDuration,p=0;for(var i=0;i<120;i++){var tt=time-i*f;if(s.valueAtTime(tt)>=th&&s.valueAtTime(tt-f)<th){p=A*Math.exp(-k*i*f);break;}}value+[p,p]; 'Audio Keyframe Layer' is a layer-type property: it cannot be set from a spec; set it with effect.property('Audio Keyframe Layer').setValue(audioAmplitudeLayer.index). cards.name: Pulse Random
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: sliders for a scale pop that re-fires at random intervals between Min Delay and Max Delay. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on Scale reads it.
use_for: Idle 'alive' pops on icons in an explainer grid so they fire out of sync
Random twinkle on map pins or data points
Background sticker pops in a reel
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing
Duplicated layers pop in unison unless the expression seeds by layer index

params.name: Min Delay
params.does: Shortest gap in seconds between pops

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Pulse Random'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): on Transform/Scale: var c=effect("Pulse Random"),lo=c("Min Delay").value,hi=c("Max Delay").value;seedRandom(index,true);var t0=0,t1=random(lo,hi);while(t1<=time){t0=t1;t1+=random(lo,hi);}var s=c("Amplitude")*Math.exp(-c("Decay")*(time-t0));value+[s,s]; Decay's harvested minimum is 4 (not 0). cards.name: Radial Wipe Master Controls
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect from AE's legacy transition presets: a Transition Completion slider, Feather and two direction checkboxes meant to drive a Radial Wipe through expressions. On its own it shows nothing.
use_for: One master slider driving several Radial Wipe layers at once (pie-chart or clock-style reveal)
Clock-sweep reveal of a map or photo in a documentary
Countdown-style sweep on a timer graphic
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing; for a one-off wipe use the real Radial Wipe effect
The checkbox meanings ('...the other corner', 'counterclockwise') are inferred from their names

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: Percent of the layer wiped away
params.typical: 100 to 0 to reveal, 0 to 100 to hide

params.name: Feather
params.does: Edge softness in pixels for the driven wipe

params.name: ...the other corner
params.does: Checkbox 0/1: start from the opposite corner

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (PresetEffects.xml, one of the 'ADBE CM' transition master controls); no AE 2026 preset uses it. To use: add the real Radial Wipe (match 'ADBE Radial Wipe') to the same layer and link its properties with expressions, e.g. on Radial Wipe/Transition Completion: effect("Radial Wipe Master Controls")("Transition Completion"); on Feather: effect("Radial Wipe Master Controls")("Feather"); on the Wipe popup: effect("Radial Wipe Master Controls")("counterclockwise")==1?2:1. Usually simpler to apply 'ADBE Radial Wipe' directly and keyframe it. Premiere 2026 has no Radial Wipe video effect; nearest is the Clock Wipe video transition (the 'Radial Wipe' transition sweeps from a corner). The '...the other corner' checkbox suggests these controls were built for a corner-anchored, Premiere-style radial wipe (inferred).

cards.name: Random Fill Color
cards.summary: Control-only pseudo effect: a base colour plus hue/saturation/lightness variation and timing sliders for a fill colour that drifts randomly over time. Nothing changes on screen until an expression on a Fill colour reads it.
use_for: Colour-shifting background shapes or text boxes behind an explainer title
Party or celebration graphics in a reel
Varied colours across duplicated icons without hand-picking each
avoid: Applied alone it does nothing
Large hue variation breaks brand palettes (party saffron/green, channel colours)
Short Transition Time looks like flicker

params.name: Base Color
params.does: Centre colour the randomness varies around

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo effect (expression-control container defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, verified 2026-10-03): it renders NOTHING by itself and no preset shipped with AE 2026 references it. Add it with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE DE Random Fill Color'), then put an expression on the target property that reads it. Adobe's original companion expression is not shipped, so use ours (untested, JavaScript expression engine): add a Fill effect ('ADBE Fill') and on Fill/Color: var c=effect("Random Fill Color"),T=c("Transition Time"),b=rgbToHsl(c("Base Color")),n=Math.floor(time/T);function col(k){seedRandom(index*977+k,true);var h=b[0]+random(-1,1)*c("Max Hue Variation")/360;return hslToRgb([(h%1+1)%1,clamp(b[1]+random(-1,1)*c("Max Saturation Variation")/100,0,1),clamp(b[2]+random(-1,1)*c("Max Lightness Variation")/100,0,1),1]);}ease(time-n*T,0,T,col(n),col(n+1)); (Transition Time Variation and the Random Start checkboxes are ignored by this expression.) Simpler shipped alternative: apply the preset 'Random Colors.ffx' (Presets/Behaviors) instead. No Premiere equivalent.
